NEW DELHI: The Congress, an ally of Tamil Nadu's ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), on Tuesday welcomed the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at its traditional spot, instead of the Deepathoon atop Thiruparankundram Hill in Madurai.In an interim one-time order passed on November 20, the Supreme Court allowed the Karthigai Deepam to be lit at the Deepathoon, instead of its usual spot above the Uchhipillaiyar temple.On Monday, the Madras high court also directed authorities to comply with the top court's order."The lamp was lit at the place where it was supposed to be lit. ... The 'Sanghi' monkeys who came to play politics at the festival of lights were left with nothing but disappointment," Tamil Nadu Congress president Manickam Tagore wrote in a Tamil-language post on X shortly after the ceremonial lighting.The ceremony took place amid tight security, with 5,618 police personnel deployed to maintain law and order. According to an official statement issued a day before the event, the security deployment was led by 12 Superintendents of Police.Additionally, prohibitory orders were imposed in Madurai ahead of the lighting.The Karthigai Deepam controversy centres on a prolonged legal dispute over the lighting of the ceremonial lamp at the Deepathoon, an ancient stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram Hill in Madurai, near the Sikandar Badhusha Dargah.The dispute began in November last year when local authorities denied permission for the hilltop ritual, citing law-and-order concerns. The Madras high court overturned the decision in December 2025.A division bench of the high court upheld the decision in January and directed that the ceremony be conducted in coordination with the police and the Archaeological Survey of India.The Tamil Nadu government subsequently moved the Supreme Court, which issued a notice on the state's plea in August. The top court later permitted the lamp to be lit at the Deepathoon, but its order was ultimately not implemented.
Article Summary: The Congress welcomed the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at its traditional spot, instead of the Deepathoon atop Thiruparankundram Hill in Madurai. The ceremony took place amid tight security, with 5,618 police personnel deployed to maintain law and order.

NEW DELHI: The Madras HC's Madurai Bench on Tuesday directed the Tamil Nadu government and all authorities concerned to comply with the Supreme Court 's order permitting the ceremonial lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at Thiruparankundram hill. It also directed the officials to release all persons unlawfully detained under Thiruparankundram prohibitory orders.The direction was issued to the district collector, police commissioner and temple authorities amid heightened security and restrictions ahead of the ceremony.The court's intervention came amid a dispute over the implementation of the apex court's November 20 order, which permitted a one-time lighting of the lamp at the hilltop Deepathoon.The state informed the HC that 258 persons have detained apprehending disorder based on intelligence and past conduct.Meanwhile, Tamil Nadu BJP president Nainar Nagenthran, who was placed under house arrest while attempting to visit Thiruparankundram, accused the police of preventing him from exercising his fundamental rights."In the absence of any legally valid prohibitory order, the police are preventing me from visiting the temple to offer prayers. Preventing us from leaving our homes in the name of arrest amounts to a violation of an individual's fundamental rights," he said.Citing Articles 25 and 26 of the Constitution, Nagenthran said citizens had the right to worship according to their faith and freely practise religious activities."However, these fundamental rights are being denied in Tamil Nadu. Despite the Supreme Court's directions, how can restrictions on lighting the ceremonial lamp and offering prayers at sacred places such as Thiruparankundram be justified?" he said.He also alleged that around 200 police personnel had been deployed outside his residence since morning and that police vehicles followed him even when he attempted to drop his children at school."Such acts of oppression are taking place only in Tamil Nadu and are not witnessed in any other state," he said.Nagenthran further accused the state government of using the restrictions to divert public attention from other issues, including sexual harassment allegations against ruling party members and MLAs and the Kallakurichi incident.The dispute centres on a demand by Hindu groups and a section of devotees to light a traditional oil lamp at the Deepathoon, a stone pillar on the upper reaches of Thiruparankundram hill, during the annual Karthigai Deepam festival.The issue has been contested for more than three decades through representations to temple authorities, government-facilitated peace meetings and legal proceedings.The Supreme Court, in its November 20 interim order, permitted a one-time ceremonial lighting of the lamp at the hilltop Deepathoon on November 24, near the Sikkander Badusha Dargah. It directed that the ceremony be conducted by an authorised team and barred the general public, processions and gatherings at the hilltop site to maintain law and order.The Tamil Nadu government moved the Supreme Court seeking a review of its interim order.The Madurai district administration had imposed prohibitory orders from November 23 night until November 25 morning, banning public gatherings, rallies and unauthorised climbing of the hill. Security was also tightened, with more than 5,600 police personnel deployed across the hill and surrounding areas.
Article Summary: Madras HC directs Tamil Nadu officials to follow the Supreme Court's Deepam lighting order amid heightened tensions. Tamil Nadu BJP president Nainar Nagenthran, who was placed under house arrest while attempting to visit Thiruparankundram, accused police of preventing him from exercising his fundamental rights.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu BJP president Nainar Nagenthran was placed under house arrest on Tuesday while he was on his way to Thirupparankundram for the Karthigai Deepam festival, amid heightened security over the proposed lighting of a lamp at the hilltop Deepathoon.Several BJP leaders and members of Hindu organisations were also detained across the state as police enforced restrictions ahead of the ceremony permitted by the Supreme Court.Condemning the police action, Nagenthran questioned the deployment of a large security force and the detention of party workers and Hindu groups."Deploying over 10,000 policemen is unnecessary, many Hindus, BJP cadres kept under house arrest, we condemn it," he said.Nagenthran planned to visit Thirupparankundram to check whether the lamp would be lit in accordance with the Supreme Court's order. Police personnel were deployed outside his residence in Tirunelveli, news agency PTI reported citing party sources.The BJP said scores of its leaders and cadres, along with members of the Hindu Munnani organisation, were detained to prevent them from travelling to Madurai and checking whether the SC directive was being implemented.In Sivaganga, several Hindu Munnani leaders and members were detained. Police also detained right-wing activists in other parts of Tamil Nadu.The Madurai district administration imposed prohibitory orders from 9pm on November 23 until 10am on November 25, banning public gatherings, rallies and unauthorised climbing of Thirupparankundram hill. However, customary worship, routine temple rituals, lawful access to the dargah and activities implementing Supreme Court directions were exempted.Around 5,618 police personnel, including 12 SPs, eight ASPs and 132 inspectors, were deployed across the hill, temple steps, Girivalam path and surrounding areas.The police also barricaded the Deepathoon and deployed personnel to guard the structure. More than 70 CCTV and facial-recognition cameras were installed, while drone operations were prohibited in the area for two days.The dispute centres on the demand by Hindu groups and a section of devotees to light a traditional oil lamp at the Deepathoon, a stone pillar on the upper reaches of Thirupparankundram hill, during the annual Karthigai Deepam festival.The demand has been pursued for more than three decades through representations to temple authorities, government-facilitated peace meetings and legal proceedings.The Subramanya Swamy temple is situated at the foothills, while a Dargah is located near the hilltop. A Shiva temple is also situated on the hill. Hindu groups maintain that the stone pillar where they seek to light the lamp belongs to the temple, citing civil court decisions dating back about a century.Dargah officials and Muslim organisations have opposed the proposed lighting, citing its proximity to their place of worship. The dispute involves questions of ownership and the rights of the respective parties.On November 20, the Supreme Court permitted a one-time ceremonial lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at the hilltop Deepathoon on November 24, near the Sikkander Badusha Dargah.The apex court specified that the ceremony must be carried out by an authorised team. It barred the general public, processions and gatherings at the hilltop site to maintain law and order.Meanwhile, the Madras HC's Madurai Bench, led by Justice G R Swaminathan, summoned officials amid the restrictions imposed by the district administration.
Article Summary: Several leaders detained, security tightened at Thirupparankundram hill. The dispute centres on the demand by Hindu groups and a section of devotees to light a traditional oil lamp at the Deepathoon. The demand has been pursued for more than three decades through representations to temple authorities, government- facilitated peace meetings and legal proceedings.

NEW DELHI: BJP leader and former Union minister Sanjeev Balyan on Tuesday said the "ghosts of the Muzaffarnagar riots" continue to haunt Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Azam Khan , adding that he cannot escape responsibility for the violence.Speaking to PTI, Balyan was responding to questions about Azam Khan's recent release from jail, the SP veteran's allegations that the BJP-led Uttar Pradesh government was targeting him, and whether his return could influence Muslim voters ahead of the 2027 assembly elections in the state." I enjoy listening to Azam Khan's interviews. He speaks interestingly and often expresses his pain, saying this or that happened to him. But perhaps he does not remember the pain he caused us," the former Muzaffarnagar MP told PTI.Balyan alleged that 6,250 people were named in cases related to the Muzaffarnagar riots on Azam Khan's instructions, with thousands subsequently sent to jail."The ghost of the Muzaffarnagar riots continues to haunt Azam Khan, whether those who died were Hindus or Muslims. Most of those who were jailed were Hindus. Perhaps he has been facing the consequences of those actions for the past 10 years," the BJP leader said."Those who lost their lives in the Muzaffarnagar riots, whether Hindus or Muslims, and the families affected by the violence cannot be forgotten. Azam Khan cannot escape responsibility for what happened," he added.Balyan also dismissed Azam Khan's allegations of "political revenge", saying his legal troubles were not the result of vendetta but stemmed from his "past actions".Balyan acknowledged that Azam Khan's return could consolidate Muslim votes in favour of the SP in western Uttar Pradesh but maintained that the BJP does not receive significant support from Muslim voters."Perhaps I received the highest number of Muslim votes in the Lok Sabha elections, but I still lost. How much support Azam Khan will get and how much Owaisi will get is something only time will tell," he said, referring to the 2024 Lok Sabha polls.Muzaffarnagar in western Uttar Pradesh witnessed communal riots in August-September 2013, when the Samajwadi Party government, led by then chief minister Akhilesh Yadav, was in power.Azam Khan, a 10-time MLA from Rampur, served as a cabinet minister in the SP government from 2012 to 2017. He held key portfolios, including parliamentary affairs and urban development, and was considered one of the most influential figures in the state government.He was released from jail on November 18 after the Allahabad high court granted him interim bail in an Enforcement Directorate (ED) money laundering case linked to his Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur.The ED had arrested him on October 31, shortly after he was released from Rampur jail in another case. He had spent nearly 11 months in jail during his previous stint, which ended on October 31.On November 19, the Supreme Court refused to interfere with the high court order and dismissed the ED's plea challenging Azam Khan's interim bail.
Article Summary: BJP leader Sanjeev Balyan says the "ghosts of the Muzaffarnagar riots" continue to haunt Samajwadi Party (SP) leader Azam Khan. He says Khan cannot escape responsibility for the violence, adding that 6,250 people were named in cases related to the riots on Khan's instructions. He also dismissed Khan's allegations of "political revenge", saying his legal troubles were not the result of vendetta.

NEW DELHI: The renewed alliance between the Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections drew sharp reactions from opposition leaders on Tuesday. Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal accused the two parties of coming together for power and the Congress calling the tie-up opportunistic.The criticism came after Union home minister Amit Shah, BJP president Nitin Nabin and SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal formally announced the alliance at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi. Shah said the two parties would contest all 117 Assembly seats in Punjab, ahead of the 2027 assembly elections, with the SAD to get the chief minister's post.Addressing a joint press conference, Shah said the two parties had decided to fight the Punjab elections together and confirmed that the SAD would rejoin the NDA.“Both the BJP and the Akali Dal have decided to fight the Punjab Assembly elections together and the Akali Dal will also join the NDA from today. This is a great occasion that on Guru Purab the Akali Dal, one of our oldest allies is returning to the NDA,” Shah said.Reacting to the announcement, Kejriwal said the BJP and SAD had repeatedly joined hands and parted ways for political convenience.“Our alliance is with the mothers and daughters of Punjab. Our alliance is with the SC community of Punjab.Our alliance is with the farmers of Punjab. Our alliance is with the traders of Punjab,” Kejriwal said, alleging that political parties come together for power, part ways and reunite.“These people come together for the sake of power, then part ways, and then come together again. We, on the other hand, are working for the development of Punjab. All of Punjab can see how, over the past five years, Bhagwant Mann has worked diligently to try and set things right, to repair the damage inflicted upon Punjab over the last 70–75 years,” he said.“When we spoke to the PM about the expansion of the NDA, he called Sukhbir Badal and said that the NDA is now complete. The Akali Dal and the BJP have a long relationship and this alliance is a symbol of brotherhood and we will move forward together,” Shah said, while announcing the alliance on Tuesday.Meanwhile, Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh termed the alliance a “directionless” tie-up, alleging that the two parties had reunited out of “greed” for power and lacked an agenda for Punjab's development.Reacting to the announcement, Singh told PTI, “The reunion between the SAD and the BJP is only for the greed for power.”“They have no development agenda for Punjab or roadmap for the state's progress. They have joined hands merely for their own development. They have joined hands again with a single motive to capture power in Punjab,” he said, asserting that neither party stood a chance of forming the next government.Singh also asked Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) chief Sukhbir Singh Badal to explain to the people why he had quit the NDA in 2020.AAP leader Jarnail Singh also criticised the reunion, saying, “Zero plus zero will always remain zero. The Akali Dal and the BJP have no future in Punjab, as the people of the state have overwhelmingly rejected both parties for several reasons.”He said people would not forget how more than 700 farmers lost their lives during the protests against the Centre's farm laws. “They will also never forget the sacrilege of the Guru Granth Sahib during the Akali Dal government,” he said.“These two parties, both discredited in the eyes of the people, cannot succeed by joining hands,” Jarnail Singh added.Earlier, Amarinder Singh Raja Warring had also criticised the proposed alliance before its formal announcement. Warring accused Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) leaders Sukhbir Singh Badal and Harsimrat Kaur Badal of misleading voters over their political ties with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), questioning why the two parties had split in 2020.“Sukhbir Badal and Harsimrat Kaur Badal are trying to fool people. Whenever there was a vote in Parliament on issues such as the Presidential election or the Uniform Civil Code, they would stand with the BJP. But when they came here, they would claim that they had no alliance with the BJP. Why did they break the alliance in the first place?” Warring said.Referring to the Centre's three farm laws, he alleged that the Akali Dal initially supported the legislation before changing its position following protests by farmers.Meanwhile, HM Shah outlined the alliance's priorities, identifying the eradication of drugs and corruption and the strengthening of nationalist forces in Punjab as key goals. He announced a deadline for making the state drug-free.Additionally, “Shah said the BJP and SAD would contest all 117 seats in the Punjab Assembly elections. He also indicated that the chief minister's post would go to the SAD as part of the alliance arrangement.”The BJP and SAD ended their alliance in 2020 after the Akali Dal withdrew from the NDA over the Centre's three farm laws, which were subsequently repealed. The parties contested the 2022 Assembly elections separately.Their electoral fortunes had declined in the years after their split. In 2017, the SAD won 15 seats and the BJP three, while in 2022 the SAD secured three seats and the BJP two. The AAP won 92 seats in 2022.
Article Summary: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal accused the two parties of coming together for power. Union home minister Amit Shah, BJP president Nitin Nabin and SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal formally announced the alliance at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi.

Article Title: Six dead as powerful explosion rips through restaurant in Vietnam; several homes damaged
Article Text:
Suspected gas explosion rips through Hanoi eatery in Vietnam

At least six people were killed and 10 others injured after a powerful explosion ripped through a restaurant in Hanoi, Vietnam, on Tuesday morning. The blast partially brought down the building, damaged several neighbouring houses and left rescue teams searching the rubble amid fears that more people could be trapped underneath.Police suspect the blast was caused by a gas leak, but an investigation is underway.The explosion occurred around 8 am at an eatery on Nguyen Van Tuyet Street in the Dong Da district of the Vietnamese capital, according to reports by Vietnamese media outlet VnExpress.The Vietnamese outlet reported that the explosion shattered windows, cracked walls and tore metal shutters from their frames. Corrugated metal roofs and awnings also collapsed, while debris was scattered across the street. The Independent reported that around 10 houses within a 15-metre radius were damaged, with debris strewn across more than 20 metres of the road.Police said preliminary findings pointed to a gas explosion, though investigations into the exact cause were continuing.The Hanoi Department of Health said 10 injured people were receiving emergency treatment at three hospitals — Saint Paul General Hospital, Dong Da General Hospital and Hanoi Medical University Hospital — The Independent reported.One victim died at Dong Da General Hospital after being struck by flying debris. Preliminary reports indicated that he had been walking past the restaurant when the explosion occurred.The Independent reported that local residents helped pull the bodies of victims from beneath the rubble. Authorities were concerned that more people could be trapped, as the restaurant was open when the blast struck.Police were using detection equipment to search for survivors and hydraulic machinery to lift concrete slabs. Residents of neighbouring buildings considered structurally unsafe were also being relocated.The blast shook nearby apartment buildings and houses, with residents reporting damage to their homes. Lan Phuong, 26, told VnExpress that the explosion jolted her and her younger sister awake and sent their balcony door flying about three metres.“Luckily, we were both covered by blankets at the time and were not seriously injured. But we were terrified and could only scream,” she said.Police are continuing search and rescue operations and investigating the suspected gas leak.
Article Summary: At least six people were killed and 10 others injured after a powerful explosion ripped through a restaurant in Hanoi, Vietnam. The blast partially brought down the building, damaged several neighbouring houses and left rescue teams searching the rubble. Police suspect the blast was caused by a gas leak, but an investigation is underway.

NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir Police on Tuesday stopped PDP president and former chief minister Mehbooba Mufti from proceeding towards Sheshnag lake in Anantnag district amid reports of heavy machinery and excavators being deployed near the ecologically fragile glacial lake.According to news agency PTI, Mehbooba, accompanied by party MLAs Waheed Para and Syed Muntazir Mehndi, had set out in the morning towards Sheshnag along the Amarnath Yatra route in south Kashmir.The PDP leaders attempted to trek from Chandanwari to the lake but were stopped by police."My worst fears were confirmed today when police stopped me from proceeding towards Sheshnag. The questions surrounding construction in this fragile glacial ecosystem are only growing louder," Mehbooba said in social media post on X."What is being concealed today could become a man made disaster tomorrow. The Amarnath Cave, Yatra and surrounding mountains must be protected as one ecological whole," she added.The PDP president also said that the lake held a special place in Hindu tradition and described the annual Amarnath Yatra as a centuries-old symbol of Kashmiriyat and Hindu-Muslim brotherhood."The information we are receiving about what is happening there in Sheshnag is very terrifying that they have taken huge machines and huge bulldozers to Sheshnag, which is a few kilometres away from the Amarnath Ji cave, and excavation is taking place there," she said."If you destroy Jammu and Kashmir's environment, its glaciers, its mountains, and its forests like this, and take such huge machines up there, then how will this Shivling manifest? Then what will you come here for?" she added.She also alleged that the authorities were using the pretext of "development" and the pilgrimage to "alter the landscape", drawing parallels with environmental damage in Uttarakhand."You ruined the situation in Uttarakhand as well; there too, you turned pilgrimage tourism, a matter of faith, into a tourist destination. You are doing the same thing here," she said.Appealing to Union minister for road transport and highways Nitin Gadkari to intervene and review the project plans, the PDP chief urged the government to protect Kashmir's fragile Himalayan ecology."Besides our environment, these Himalayan mountains, the forests, and our glaciers, Jammu and Kashmir has nothing else," she said, adding that previous administrations had prioritised environmental preservation along the route.Amid criticism from political parties, the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) has said it is carrying out post-Amarnath Yatra works in compliance with all applicable safety norms and environmental safeguards and that its primary objective is to safeguard pilgrims throughout the yatra.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday welcomed the Shiromani Akali Dal 's (SAD) return to the National Democratic Alliance ( NDA ), as the BJP and its former ally announced a tie-up for the upcoming Punjab assembly elections . PM Modi described the partnership as a "natural alliance" and said it would work towards Punjab's development and the welfare of its people. The reunion ends a six-year break in their alliance."Putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first! I am extremely delighted that the Shiromani Akali Dal returns to the NDA family and that too on the Parkash Purab of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji," PM Modi said in a post on X."Ours is a natural alliance that will ensure Punjab gets pro-people governance that takes the state to new heights of progress. Nurtured by Atal Ji, Advani Ji and Sardar Parkash Singh Badal Ji, the Akali Dal-BJP Alliance has stood the test of time. I am confident that our Alliance will emerge as the preferred choice of the people of Punjab," he added.The BJP and SAD announced their alliance at a press conference, with Union home minister Amit Shah confirming that the two parties would contest all 117 assembly seats in Punjab.Shah said the chief minister's post would go to the SAD, which would be the "big brother" in the alliance. He added that the two parties would finalise a detailed manifesto soon.Shah said the alliance would focus on eliminating the drug menace, addressing farmers' concerns and promoting Hindu-Sikh unity."The BJP's promise of resolving farmer issues and promoting Hindu-Sikh unity will get a boost with SAD joining hands with us," he said.SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal described the tie-up as an "emotional alliance" and said the parties would work to resolve Punjab's issues, including drug abuse.Badal expressed confidence that the alliance would win more than 100 seats and predicted that the Aam Aadmi Party's tally would fall to single digits.BJP president Nitin Nabin said the partnership was a natural alliance aimed at the benefit of Punjab's people and the state's development. He said seat-sharing discussions would take place soon.The reunion comes six years after the SAD ended its 24-year alliance with the BJP in September 2020 over the Centre's three farm laws. The party withdrew from the NDA amid widespread protests by farmers against the legislation. The laws were subsequently repealed.SAD leader and then Union minister Harsimrat Kaur Badal also resigned from the Modi government.Shah said the farm laws had since been withdrawn and there was no reason for them to become an issue in the renewed alliance.Speculation about a reunion gained momentum after Sukhbir Singh Badal met Modi at Parliament House in August. Shah subsequently predicted an NDA government in Punjab during his recent visits and public remarks.Elections to the 117-member Punjab assembly are due early next year.
Article Summary: PM Modi welcomes SAD back to NDA after six years, calling the BJP-Akali partnership a time-tested alliance. PM Modi described the partnership as a "natural alliance" and said it would work towards Punjab's development and the welfare of its people. The reunion ends a six-year break in their alliance.

Article Title: Civic bodies selective on illegal constructions: SC
Article Text:
A bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and Sanjeev Sachdeva said that municipal corporations were selective in taking action

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Monday expressed concern over the menace of unauthorised construction in cities across the country with the connivance of municipal authorities but said that it may not be practical and feasible for it to monitor action taken against them.A bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and Sanjeev Sachdeva said that municipal corporations were selective in taking action as they allowed some persons to breach building bye-laws and construct beyond sanctioned plans. "We are disturbed to note the flagrant violation throughout the country," the order statedSome citizens violate and get away with it while the others follow the law and are under compulsion of the law? Why shouldn't everybody be under the compulsion of the law? Why are municipal corporations allowing certain sections of persons to breach the building bylaws in the matter of construction, go beyond the sanction plan..? It is hand in glove with those citizens. We are not mincing words, we know what is happening," the bench said.It said that the rule of law has been rendered hollow with authorities failing to enforce the law. "We are also conscious that the rule of law is rendered hollow when the authority charged with enforcing it does not enforce it. The state of municipal inspection in our cities is in a shambles, to say the least. It is often undertaken after the building has risen and the violation has become a fait accompli.Such inspections are, to say the least, a sham. It is also an open secret that unauthorised construction often flourishes with the active connivance of the municipal authorities hoping that state govts would ultimately regularise the same particularly before an impending election," the SC bench said.The court said municipal laws and building regulations differ from state to state and that any order passed by it could not necessarily be applied across the country. The bench said the court is interested in examining the larger systemic issue: failures by municipal authorities and asked state govts and Union Territories to suggest measures to address the situation.
Article Summary: A bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and Sanjeev Sachdeva said that municipal corporations were selective in taking action. It said that the rule of law has been rendered hollow with authorities failing to enforce the law. The bench said the court is interested in examining the larger systemic issue: failures by municipal authorities.

SRINAGAR: Amid criticism from political parties over deployment of an excavator near the high-altitude Sheshnag Lake, a high-risk glacial lake in J&K’s Anantnag district, the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) has said it is carrying out post-Amarnath Yatra works in compliance with all applicable safety norms and environmental safeguards and that its primary objective is to safeguard pilgrims throughout the yatra.However, the clarification did little to douse the fire.“Sheshnag is not a construction site. It is a fragile Himalayan ecosystem and a sacred lake for both Hindus and Muslims,” Congress MP and spokesperson Pawan Khera said.He said Sheshnag is among the 14 high-risk glacial lakes identified in Jammu & Kashmir. “The recent glacier-related disasters in Nepal should have been a stark warning: disturbing fragile Himalayan ecosystems can have catastrophic consequences. According to Hindu mythology, Lord Shiva left his serpents on the banks of the lake to guard the path to Amarnath, where he would reveal the Amar Katha to Goddess Parvati,” he said.“In Kashmir’s Islamic tradition, too, human beings are entrusted with stewardship of God’s creation. Protecting nature and preventing wastage are moral and religious duties. There is no Hindu-Muslim divide here. Both faiths demand the preservation of Sheshnag,” Khera added.CPM legislator M Y Tarigami said, “Visuals showing an excavator cutting and levelling earth near the lake, reportedly for road development along the Amarnath Yatra track, are deeply disturbing. Sheshnag is surrounded by loose moraine and steep slopes. Disturbing this fragile terrain with heavy machinery is an invitation to disaster.”PDP‘s Muntazir Mehdi echoed similar sentiments. “Sheshnag is not an ordinary construction site. Any careless intervention here can have consequences far beyond the site itself, affecting the lake, its catchment and the water systems downstream,” he said.Hurriyat Conference chairman Mirwaiz Umar Farooq said those governing owe answers to people for the serious environmental concerns created by such “developmental projects.” “Our precious mountains, glaciers and water bodies need protection, not plunder, for now and for the future generations.So, this must be immediately stopped.”The BRO said the video circulating on social media claims about new works is incorrect.“Based on experience of previous Yatra and requirement highlighted for wider road for Shri Amarnath ji yatra, BRO has started widening of tracks focusing on stabilising vulnerable stretches and widening the tracks as prescribed to ease congestion and allow safer passage,” it said.
Article Summary: Border Roads Organisation (BRO) has said it is carrying out post-Amarnath Yatra works in compliance with all applicable safety norms and environmental safeguards. The clarification did little to douse the fire over deployment of an excavator near the high-altitude Sheshnag Lake in J&K’s Anantnag district.

Article Title: NIA court frees 4 held for 2020 Srinagar terror attack that killed 2 soldiers
Article Text:
Special NIA judge Manjeet Rai ordered their release forthwith if they were not required in any other case.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: The killing of two Army soldiers in a Nov 2020 terrorist attack on the outskirts of Srinagar was established, but the prosecution failed to prove that the four arrested men had helped the terrorists, a special NIA court said Monday while acquitting them under UAPA.Special NIA judge Manjeet Rai acquitted Nasir Ahmad Dar, Zahid Ahmad Allai, Usman Ahmad Sheikh and Humayun Ahmad Sheikh of charges under sections 13, 18, 19 and 39 of UAPA. He ordered their release forthwith if they were not required in any other case.The court said there was no evidence that the accused conspired with, sheltered or supported the terrorists, communicated with them or were present near the attack site. No arms, explosives or other material were found in their possession, making the statutory presumption under section 43E of UAPA inapplicable.The prosecution case rested entirely on circumstantial evidence, with no eyewitness linking the four men to the attack. Citing Supreme Court’s 1984 judgement in Sharad Birdhichand Sarda vs State of Maharashtra, NIA court reiterated that every circumstance in a case based on circumstantial evidence must be fully established and the chain must point exclusively to the accused’s guilt.The court said prosecution had established that the attack killed two soldiers and a service rifle was lost, but the gravity of the crime could not substitute for legal proof.“The loss of lives is a grave one and the anxiety of the prosecuting agency to bring every person responsible to book is understandable. But the law requires that guilt be proved by legal evidence and the gravity of the crime only heightens the need for such proof,” it said.The four men are residents of Zainakote, where the attacked happened near the HMT factory on Nov 26, 2020, when terrorists fired at an Army road opening party, killing constable Rattan Singh and sepoy Des Raj. The attackers took away a service rifle.Police registered an FIR, naming seven accused. The four men were arrested after questioning several alleged “overground” operatives of terrorist groups. They remained in judicial custody throughout the trial and appeared before the court through video conferencing.The other three, identified as Abrar Nadeem alias Khitaab, Muslim alias Hanzala alias Babar and Asrar alias Mahmood alias Abdullah, were described as Pakistani terrorists in the chargesheet. They were killed in separate shootouts in Sopore of Baramulla district and Malura outside Srinagar in June 2021, and proceedings against them were abated. The snatched rifle was later found in a separate case in Sopore.
Article Summary: Nasir Ahmad Dar, Zahid Ahmad Allai, Usman Ahmad Sheikh and Humayun Ahmad Sheikh acquitted under UAPA. Judge Manjeet Rai ordered their release forthwith if they were not required in any other case. No evidence that the accused conspired with, sheltered or supported the terrorists.

Article Title: Can't do much for Tamil Nadu man in Russia army: Govt to SC
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Centre on Monday told the Supreme Court that it does not have much locus in ensuring the return of an Indian national who renounced his citizenship to take up Russia's and joined its army.Although Solicitor General (SG) Tushar Mehta said that govt would explore its options for the repatriation of Abinesh - a Tamil Nadu native who had gone to Moscow for studies but took up Russian citizenship there after surrendering his Indian passport - he added that Russian authorities are right in refusing information about the individual who is now enrolled in their armed forces.The apex court asked the Union govt to explore the possibility of Abinesh's return.Hearing his father's petition, a bench led by CJI Surya Kant said little is known about Abinesh's agreement with the intermediary who had arranged for his studies in Moscow. It asked the Centre if it could help now that the Russian authorities are claiming that he had renounced Indian citizenship and acquired Russian citizenship.The Solicitor General told the court that he would take instructions from the ministry concerned on what kind of humanitarian intervention could be made in this case.Months after Abinesh left for Russia for studies in April, the Indian Embassy in Moscow responded to his family, saying, "The Embassy has taken up the matter with the Ministry of Defence of the Russian Federation and requested it to release him. It may be mentioned that he has joined the Russian Army as a Russian citizen. As per the attached documents, he has willingly relinquished Indian citizenship. He has a Russian passport; the Embassy will update you as soon as a response is received from the Russian authorities.The petitioner said he was deeply concerned about the circumstances in which his son's citizenship status was reportedly changed, and military service arrangements were subsequently made. "I am unable to understand the circumstances under which he (Abinesh) acquired Russian citizenship and entered into military service within such a short period," he said.
Article Summary: The Centre told the Supreme Court that it does not have much locus in ensuring the return of an Indian national who renounced his citizenship to take up Russia's and joined its army. The apex court asked the Union govt to explore the possibility of Abinesh's return.

Article Title: SC grants bail to Godhra train burning convict on medical grounds
Article Text:
A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale suspended the sentence as Pada is suffering from serious cardiovascular disease

New Delhi: Supreme Court Monday granted bail on medical grounds to Irfan Siraj Pada, one of the convicts in the Godhra train burning case.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale suspended the sentence as Pada is suffering from serious cardiovascular disease and the state accepted his medical condition. He has been in jail for around 18 years."Counsel for state submits that condition of the petitioner as submitted by the senior counsel appearing for the petitioner is factually correct. In view of the aforementioned factual scenario, we are inclined to grant suspension of sentence to the petitioner on medical grounds," the bench said.The train burning took place on Feb 27, 2002, killing 58 people inside the S6 coach of Sabarmati Express. In March 2011, the trial court had convicted 31 people, of whom 11 were sentenced to death and the remaining 20 were awarded life in prison. Sixty-three other accused were acquitted. In 2017, Gujarat HC commuted the death sentence of the 11 convicts to life terms and upheld the life sentences awarded to the other 20. The appeals filed by the convicts in SC have been pending since 2018. TNN
Article Summary: Irfan Siraj Pada is one of the convicts in the Godhra train burning case. The train burning took place on Feb 27, 2002, killing 58 people. In March 2011, the trial court had convicted 31 people, of whom 11 were sentenced to death and the remaining 20 were awarded life in prison.

Article Title: Log out of Whatsapp Web on shared computers to avoid misuse: Govt
Article Text:
WhatsApp Web security alert: Users advised to log out after every session to prevent account misuse

NEW DELHI: Govt has warned that leaving WhatsApp Web logged in on a shared computer can expose users' accounts to unauthorised access. In an advisory, the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), under the ministry of home affairs, urged users to log out manually after every session, particularly on office computers and other devices that people can access.The advisory, issued by I4C's National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit, said someone who gains access to an active session could read private messages, view contacts and group chats, and send messages while posing as the account holder. That could give fraudsters a way to approach friends, relatives or colleagues from an account they already recognise and trust.The queries sent to Meta, which owns WhatsApp, remained unanswered.I4C said a WhatsApp Web session can remain active after the browser tab or window is closed. It advised users to avoid signing in from cyber cafes, public kiosks, hotel business centres or borrowed computers. For temporary use on a trusted computer, it recommended opening a private window and manually logging out before closing it.The advisory also urged users to avoid exchanging confidential information through WhatsApp Web. It asked them to take unexplained account activity seriously, including messages they did not send or unexpected replies from contacts. Users were also advised to keep their operating systems, browsers and security software updated and avoid suspicious downloads and untrusted applications.
Article Summary: Users advised to log out after every session to prevent account misuse. Someone who gains access to an active session could read private messages, view contacts and group chats. That could give fraudsters a way to approach friends, relatives or colleagues from an account they already recognise and trust.

Article Title: ‘Sex sells’: Trump celebrates Huang's Nvidia return with AI image of CEO holding red bra

Trump celebrates Huang's return

Scandal, chips and national security

US President Donald Trump marked Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s return with an unusual tribute on social media: an AI-generated image of Huang holding a red bra, his face bloodied, as Secret Service agents surround him.The image, posted on Trump’s Truth Social account on Monday, appeared to recreate the iconic scene of the president raising his fist after surviving an assassination attempt at a campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, in July 2024. A Nvidia flag stood behind Huang in the image, which seemed to cast the executive’s return after a personal scandal as a comeback akin to Trump’s own political resurgence.The post came hours after Nvidia’s board unanimously reinstated Huang as CEO, reversing its earlier position following revelations about his alleged relationships, including one with a woman reported to be a suspected Chinese spy.Trump had publicly been pushing for Huang’s reinstatement, congratulating Nvidia on what he called an “absolutely GREAT decision”.In a separate Truth Social post, the president said the company’s board had made the “correct and proper decision” and insisted the government had no reason to believe Huang’s return posed a national security risk.“The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the US Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct,” Trump wrote.He described Huang as a “Great Patriot and National Treasure”, while urging Nvidia to continue its internal investigation into compliance with US export controls.Huang’s reinstatement followed reports of multiple affairs, including one with a woman alleged to have been a Chinese spy. Reports also alleged relationships with at least two Nvidia employees. The allegations had raised questions about the executive’s judgment and the company’s handling of potential national security concerns.Trump, however, suggested the controversy could ultimately benefit Huang’s public image.In an interview with CNBC on Monday, the president said the scandal could be a “net positive” for the Nvidia CEO.“Sex sells, fellas,” Trump said, arguing that Huang would not be diminished by the controversy and that people respected what he had gone through.The board’s decision drew immediate criticism from lawmakers, who questioned whether the company had adequately weighed the risks. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer said Democrats would investigate Huang’s reinstatement, accusing Trump of putting his own financial interests and those of wealthy allies ahead of national security.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump marked Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s return with an unusual tribute on social media. He shared an AI-generated image of Huang holding a red bra, his face bloodied, as Secret Service agents surround him. The image appeared to recreate the iconic scene of the president raising his fist after surviving an assassination attempt at a campaign rally in July 2024. A Nvidia flag stood behind Huang in the image, which seemed to cast the executive's return after a personal scandal as a comeback akin to Trump's own political resurgence.

Article Title: Pune techie beats software engineer girlfriend to death in PG room after row over him talking to other woman
Article Text:
Software engineer allegedly murdered by boyfriend in Hinjewadi





PUNE: A software engineer (30) was arrested on Monday on the charge of allegedly beating his girlfriend to death (27), also a techie, following an argument in her rented accommodation in Hinjewadi's Sakhare Vasti.The victim's cousin, who stays in Sus, lodged a police complaint after an alert from her mother that she was not answering calls. "The accused also called police requesting an ambulance, saying that his friend was unresponsive," inspector Siddharam Mhetre said.Police said the accused allegedly remained beside the body overnight before calling the emergency helpline (112) the next morning to report the incident.On reaching the paying guest accommodation, police found the techie unconscious in her room. "We took her to hospital, where doctors declared her dead," he said.The woman was from Wardha and the accused from Hingoli. They worked in two prominent IT firms and stayed in neighbouring buildings as paying guests. "The accused admitted to have hit her. She could not withstand the blows and died," he said.DCP (Zone-II) Pradip Jadhav of Pimpri Chinchwad police said they were in a relationship for three-and-a-half years.The accused claimed that they frequently argued as she disliked him talking to other women."After returning from dinner on Sunday night, there was an argument between the two and he hit her. Around 3.30am, he again punched her in the face and banged her head against the wall. He called police around 6am," Jadhav said.The building owner said the victim had moved in about six months ago. "We learnt about the murder when police came here in the morning," the owner said.
Article Summary: A software engineer (30) was arrested on the charge of allegedly beating his girlfriend to death. Article Title: 174 IndiGo passengers fly to Bengaluru twice in three hours after aborted landing
Article Text: CHENNAI: About 174 passengers on an IndiGo flight from Chennai to Bengaluru ended up making the journey twice within a span of three hours on Monday evening after the pilot aborted the landing at Bengaluru due to an unstabilised approach and flew back to Chennai.The flight, scheduled to depart Chennai domestic airport at 4.20pm, took off at 5.06pm after a delay. It reached Bengaluru's airspace around 5.40pm but could not land. As the aircraft approached the runway, the pilot reportedly encountered an “unstabilised approach” situation and decided to abort landing and return to Chennai.The aircraft landed in Chennai at 6.10pm, leaving passengers confused about why they had been brought back to their departure airport. When passengers sought an explanation from the cabin crew, they were reportedly told that the aircraft had returned due to administrative reasons and would depart again shortly.The same aircraft subsequently took off from Chennai at 7.30pm with all 174 passengers and landed safely in Bengaluru at 8.15pm.Airport sources said the aircraft had returned to Chennai after the pilot abandoned the landing attempt in Bengaluru owing to an unstabilised approach while nearing the runway. IndiGo did not respond to clarify about the incident.
Article Summary: The flight, scheduled to depart Chennai domestic airport at 4.20pm, took off at 5.06pm after a delay. It reached Bengaluru's airspace around 5.40pm but could not land. The same aircraft subsequently took off from Chennai at 7.30pm with all 174 passengers and landed safely in Bengaluru at 8.15pm.

LUCKNOW: A 40-year-old farmer, reportedly struggling with debt and financial difficulties, died by suicide on Sunday (Nov 22), a day after his daughter’s engagement ceremony, in Mod Khurd village under Chirgaon police station limits in Jhansi district.The deceased, identified as Veer Singh Rajput, had reportedly borrowed money to conduct his 19-year-old daughter Shivani’s engagement ceremony and was worried about arranging funds for her wedding, scheduled for May 5, 2027.According to family members, Shivani’s marriage had been fixed with a man from Parichha village in the Baragaon area. Article Title: 4 children killed, 25 injured after truck rams school bus on Agra-Lucknow expressway in Kannauj
Article Text:
A tragic accident on the Agra-Lucknow Expressway claimed the lives of four school students when a truck collided with their stationary bus





LUCKNOW: Four schoolchildren were killed and 25 others injured after a speeding truck loaded with potatoes rammed into a school bus parked on the Agra-Lucknow Expressway in Kannauj district early on Tuesday. The children were returning to Kaushambi after a three-day educational and recreational tour of Agra and Mathura when the accident occurred.The bus, belonging to Oriental Public School in Kaushambi, was carrying around 60 people, including 50 students, eight teachers and two driver-cum-conductors. The students were from Classes 6 to 10.According to Kannauj Superintendent of Police Vinod Kumar, the bus had left Agra around midnight and was travelling towards Kaushambi. At around 6am, it stopped on the expressway to allow the children to use the toilet. A speeding truck approaching from behind crashed into it near milestone 210, under the jurisdiction of Thathia police station.The impact was so severe that the rear portion of the bus was completely mangled, seats were uprooted and several children became trapped between them. The collision reportedly dragged the bus for some distance, leaving passengers screaming for help.Police personnel, Uttar Pradesh Expressways Industrial Development Authority (UPEIDA) teams and local residents rushed to the spot and launched a rescue operation. The injured children were pulled out of the wreckage and taken by ambulance to the medical college in Tirwa for treatment.The four deceased students were identified as Aryan Chaurasia (14), son of Prem Kumar Chaurasia; Raziullah (16), son of Shami Ullah; Zaid Mirza (17), son of Riyaz Ahmed; and Armaan (17), son of Riyaz Ahmed. Aryan and Raziullah were in Class 8, while Zaid and Armaan were in Class 10.School manager Salman and one of the injured students sustained critical injuries and were referred to Hallet Hospital in Kanpur for advanced treatment. Their condition was reported to be serious.Police suspect that the truck driver may have dozed off at the wheel, leading to the collision. However, an injured student, Prince Prajapati, alleged that the driver had consumed alcohol before driving. The allegation is yet to be independently established and will form part of the investigation.Another student, Shakti Yadav, said the bus had stopped because one of their friends was feeling unwell and needed to use the toilet. He said the truck hit the bus at high speed, dragging it for some distance. He also claimed that the school principal was near the entrance and was dragged during the impact.The district administration reached the medical college to oversee treatment and rescue arrangements. District Magistrate Ashutosh Mohan Agnihotri and SP Vinod Kumar also visited the medical college.Children who escaped injury or sustained minor injuries were being treated before arrangements were made to send them back to Kaushambi in state roadways buses and other vehicles.Police have launched an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the accident, including the truck driver's condition, the manner in which the bus was parked on the expressway and the safety arrangements made for the return journey.The accident has once again raised concerns over road safety on expressways, particularly the risks posed by heavy vehicles allegedly driven by fatigued drivers and the safety of schoolchildren travelling overnight on long-distance trips.
Article Summary: A speeding truck loaded with potatoes rammed into a school bus parked on the Agra-Lucknow Expressway in Kannauj district early on Tuesday. The impact was so severe that the rear portion of the bus was completely mangled, seats were uprooted and several children became trapped between them. Police suspect that the truck driver may have dozed off at the wheel, leading to the collision.

Article Title: Adani power project in Satara: ‘Nod covers 4 villages, excavation on at 5th’
Article Text:
Adani Green Energy Ltd's Tarali pumped storage project is under investigation due to alleged unauthorized work at Sawarghar.





MUMBAI: Amid a row over work on Adani Green Energy Ltd’s (AGEL) 1,500MW Tarali pumped storage project beginning in Satara’s Patan taluka despite lack of approval from National Board for Wildlife (NBWL), the state forest department’s honorary wildlife warden for the district has written to Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) alleging that large-scale excavation and construction is underway in Sawarghar village, which was not listed on the environmental clearance (EC) granted by the Union forest ministry on Feb 11 last year.The honorary wildlife warden, Rohan Bhate, said the EC specified only four villages that stand to be affected—Nivade, Tondoshi, Kalambe and Jalu—in the district.A spokesperson from Adani Group said the EC covers the four villages as well as Dafalwadi, and the company later purchased private land in Sawarghar to set up temporary accommodation for workers. The company said such an accommodation was included in the project layout approval from Central Electricity Authority. It said the project has all the relevant clearances and initial works are in progress at the site.The Tarali project, estimated at Rs 5,675 crore, is planned over 150.7 hectares of private land.In his letter to MPCB member-secretary Rahul Rekhawar, Bhate claimed that the activity in Sawarghar did not have the required EC and NBWL’s approval, and sought urgent intervention and an independent investigation.Rekhawar confirmed that MPCB has received Bhate’s letter and said it is investigating the allegations.Amol Satpute, MPCB sub-regional officer in Satara, said a team from the pollution regulator inspected the Sawarghar site on Friday, where excavation was underway. Satpute said when officials questioned the site supervisor, they were told the developer was levelling land to set up a labour camp for the Tarali project. He said a report would be submitted to higher authorities.Bhate said the situation raised questions about the geographical scope and validity of the EC in relation to the work being carried out at Sawarghar. He questioned whether MPCB had verified that the proponent had obtained environmental and wildlife clearances for all land parcels involved before issuing the mandatory ‘consent to establish’ (CTE) that allows construction to begin. He said MPCB cannot distance itself from responsibility because the CTE stage is a crucial regulatory checkpoint.Bhate requested an immediate site inspection and preparation of an official panchnama by MPCB officials to document the extent of excavation and construction, the machinery deployed, and the exact location of the work. He said if any excavation or construction is found to have started without statutory approvals, authorities should register the appropriate offence and initiate legal proceedings against responsible individuals and project authorities.He also asked MPCB to determine whether activity at Sawarghar is covered by the Feb 11, 2025, EC and whether all applicable environmental permissions for that specific location have been obtained. In addition, he sought verification of whether prior approval from the NBWL’s standing committee was secured wherever legally required.Bhate said the proposed project falls within the deemed eco-sensitive zone of Koyna wildlife sanctuary and the Sahyadri tiger reserve, making strict scrutiny under environmental and wildlife protection provisions essential. He requested that the matter be assigned to an impartial higher-level authority for an independent inquiry rather than being examined only by officials linked to project clearances. Pending verification, he asked for directions to prevent any further unauthorised excavation or construction at the site.Sources said AGEL has not yet complied with the stop-work order issued on Nov 13 by Satpute, in his capacity as the Satara division’s deputy conservator of forests, for starting work on the project without NBWL’s approval. Adani Group had earlier said the proposal had been submitted to NBWL. Satpute said he would need to check whether the developer had followed the order.
Article Summary: Adani Green Energy Ltd’s 1,500MW Tarali pumped storage project is under investigation due to alleged unauthorized work at Sawarghar. Forest department's honorary wildlife warden has written to Maharashtra Pollution Control Board alleging that large-scale excavation and construction is underway.

Article Title: Buffs break away from fight, charge at 8-year-old boy, trample him to death in Ujjain
Article Text:
Eight-year-old boy named Yuvraj was killed by charging buffaloes during a traditional fight in Ujjain.





UJJAIN: In a tragic turn of events, an eight-year-old boy was trampled to death by charging buffaloes while watching a buffalo fight with his father on Friday. The incident took place at Hamukhedi on Dewas Road, in the Nagjhiri police station area of Madhya Pradesh’s Ujjain district.The buffalo fight, it turns out, is a traditional event held on the occasion of Dev Prabodhini Ekadashi, a calendar festival.The bout between two buffaloes was being staged in a field near the govt school. Around 2 pm, Akash arrived with his son Yuvraj to catch the fight. He stood at the edge of the crowd, while the boy sat close to him, eating poha (a popular local snack).As the buffaloes, released from their pen or enclosure, charged towards the spectators, one climbed onto Yuvraj’s chest. His father jumped to his rescue, and was joined by some bystanders who eventually helped pull the child out from under the marauding feet of the buffs.The boy was rushed to a hospital where the doctors declared him dead on arrival.Akash, a taxi driver, said Yuvraj, a Class 3 student, was his only son. “The buffaloes were in a fight and had locked horns. My son was sitting close to me as we watched the fight. However, all of a sudden, the buffaloes came charging in our direction and trampled my child,” the father said, laying the blame on the organiser.A private hospital in Chandesari declared him dead on arrival, after which his body was taken to the district hospital at Charak Bhawan, where a post-mortem was conducted before the last remains were handed to the family.Nagjhiri station in-charge Rakesh Bharti said such events are illegal, adding that the incident was being investigated. He said the organiser had been warned two days earlier and had promised not to hold the event, yet went ahead with it.A case of unnatural death was registered, the officer said, adding that a criminal case will be filed against the accused once the inquiry establishes the facts. Statements from the family are yet to be recorded.Local residents said a similar event three to four years ago had led to stone pelting at the police.
Article Summary: Eight-year-old trampled to death by charging buffaloes during a traditional fight in Ujjain. Incident took place at Hamukhedi on Dewas Road, in the Nagjhiri police station area of Madhya Pradesh’s UJJain district.

Article Title: Man poses as Lawrence kin to extort Delhi bizman
Article Text:
A businessman has come forward with disturbing claims of extortion threats, where he was asked for Rs 60 lakh, accompanied by a half-cut Rs 10 note as a chilling message

Extortion plan hatched to meet financial need





NEW DELHI: A half-cut, laminated Rs 10 note delivered in an envelope through a bike taxi rider provided Delhi Police with the crucial lead in cracking a bizarre Rs 60-lakh extortion attempt targeting a Janakpuri businessman.The suspect, Ashu Maurya (27), allegedly posed as Anmol Bishnoi, brother of gangster Lawrence Bishnoi , hoping the name would intimidate the family into paying up. A native of UP's Rae Bareli, he was arrested after cops tracked a trail of CCTV footage and mobile phone records.Also Read| Murders, kidnappings, extortion: Lawrence Bishnoi aide Goldy Brar on FBI's 10 most wanted fugitive list DCP (West) Hareshwar V Swami said the case came to light after businessman Jatin Gaba approached Janakpuri police, alleging his family had received WhatsApp mess-ages demanding Rs 60 lakh. The threats were accompanied by an unusual form of identification — an envelope addressed to Gaba, containing half of a laminated Rs 10 note, which was delivered to his residence.Police sources said the suspect had allegedly instructed the businessman to route the extortion money through hawala and hand it over to a person carrying the other half of the note, which was intended to serve as a verification marker.Investigators scanned CCTV footage from the house and surrounding areas and identified bike taxi rider Pankaj Gautam (22) as the person who delivered the envelope.During questioning, Gautam told police that an online ride had been booked from Manesar in Gurgaon for delivering the envelope.That disclosure led investigators to another mobile number linked to the handset allegedly used in the crime. Technical analysis showed that the number was registered in Maurya’s name, following which he was traced and arrested.During interrogation, Maurya told police that he had hatched the extortion plan to meet his financial needs. Investigators also discovered that he was famili-ar with the complainant’s family: his father had worked as the businessman’s driver for 27 years.Police said Maurya allegedly used his knowledge of the family to target them and invoked Anmol Bishnoi’s name to instil fear.The accused allegedly laminated a Rs 10 note, cut it in half and placed one portion in the envelope delivered to Gaba’s house. Threatening WhatsApp messages demanding Rs 60 lakh were also allegedly sent to the businessman’s wife, police said.Police recovered four mobile phones, a SIM card allegedly used in the crime, a tablet, a motorcycle and the other half of the laminated Rs 10 note from Maurya.
Article Summary: A half-cut, laminated Rs 10 note delivered in an envelope through a bike taxi rider provided Delhi Police with the crucial lead in cracking a bizarre Rs 60-lakh extortion attempt targeting a Janakpuri businessman. The suspect, Ashu Maurya (27), allegedly posed as Anmol Bishnoi, brother of gangster Lawrence Bish noi, hoping the name would intimidate the family into paying up.

Article Title: Rajasthan couple murdered by relative over vacating rented room
Article Text:
Couple killed by a distant relative following their request for him to leave his rental space





RAJKOT: A couple were killed and two of their relatives seriously injured when a distant relative of theirs attacked them with a nail-studded wooden club, as he held a grudge about being given notice to vacate the room they had rented to him, in Jangvad village of Jasdan taluka on Thursday.According to the FIR registered at Atkot police station on Friday, the deceased are Vilas Ghodakiya (32) and her husband, Prakash (35). The injured include the complainant, Labhu Ghodakiya (35), Prakash’s sister-in-law, and Puri, the wife of Labhu’s nephew.Atkot police arrested the accused, Ashok Ghodakiya, a resident of the same village, on charges of murder.Talking to TOI, Jasdan assistant superintendent of police Naveen Chakravarthy Repudi said the accused was unemployed and had been given a room to stay by the victims. “When they asked him to vacate the room, he held a grudge about it. He later attacked them with a club which had nails in it, which caused grievous head injuries to the victims,” he said.According to Labhu’s complaint, around 3.30pm on Thursday, she had gone to Prakash’s house to bring back her young son, Vraj, There was a knock on the door and when. Vilas opened it they and saw Ashok — a distant cousin of Prakash’s — carrying a wooden club.He began hurling abuses.When Labhu and Vilas objected to his language, Ashok allegedly threatened to kill them and swung the club at Labhu’s head. She suffered an injury to her left palm while trying to block the first blow, before a second strike hit the left side of her head.When Vilas intervened to save Labhu, Ashok struck her repeatedly on the head with the club. Hearing their screams, Prakash rushed out, followed by Puri, who was sitting at a kirana shop behind the house. Both were allegedly hit on their heads until they collapsed.The accused fled after Labhu’s eldest brother-in-law, Ramesh, arrived. The two injured victims are getting treatment at a hospital.
Article Summary: Vilas Ghodakiya (32) and her husband, Prakash (35), were killed in Jangvad village of Jasdan taluka on Thursday. The injured include the complainant, Labhu Ghodkiya (35) and Puri, the wife of Labhu’s nephew. Atkot police arrested the accused, Ashok Godakiya, on charges of murder.

Article Title: Bihar horror: Student dragged, molested; male friend assaulted, 3 arrested after video surfaces
Article Text:
Muzaffarpur district witnessed a rapid police response as three men were arrested within 12 hours for the alleged molestation of a student





PATNA: Police arrested three men within 12 hours of an incident in which a student was allegedly molested, assaulted and verbally abused in the Bochahan police station area of Muzaffarpur district.A video of the incident reportedly circulated on social media, prompting police to launch an investigation and identify the accused.The arrested men were identified as Anurag Kumar, son of Shivnath Sharma and a resident of Ward No. 1 in Kashirampur village; Vishal Kumar, son of Ram Kumar Sharma; and Ujjwal Kumar, son of Lal Babu Rai, a resident of Bhorhan village. All three were taken to Bochahan police station for questioning before being formally booked in the case.Alay Vats, Sub-Divisional Police Officer (East-I), said the incident came to light on November 19 after the video surfaced on social media."In the video, the accused molested the girl and indulged in indecent behaviour, while her friend was assaulted. Taking the matter seriously, officers began verifying the footage, examined the circumstances of the incident and identified those involved. Following the investigation and verification of the location, a police team conducted raids and apprehended all three accused within 12 hours," he said.Police also seized two mobile phones allegedly used to record and circulate the video. An FIR was registered under relevant sections of the law, and the process of sending the arrested men to judicial custody was initiated.Bochahan SHO Yashwant Kumar Mishra said police acted immediately after receiving information about the incident and intensified efforts to identify and arrest the accused. He confirmed that three men had been arrested, two mobile phones seized and further investigation was under way.The arrests were made by a team from Bochahan police station under the supervision of SDPO East-I, with the SHO leading the operation.
Article Summary: Muzaffarpur district witnessed a rapid police response as three men were arrested within 12 hours for the alleged molestation of a student. A video of the incident reportedly circulated on social media, prompting police to launch an investigation and identify the accused. The arrested men were identified as Anurag Kumar, Vishal Kumar and Ujjwal Kumar.

Article Text:
Shiv Sena (UBT) has offered a reward in response to similar announcements made by rival factions

Row over Balasaheb Thackeray's photograph

PIMPRI CHINCHWAD: Shiv Sena (UBT) has announced a reward of Rs 71,000 for anyone who slaps Shiv Sena leader Shaina NC, escalating the political row over an incident involving a photograph of party founder Balasaheb Thackeray.Making the announcement on Thursday, Shiv Sena (UBT)'s Pimpri Chinchwad unit president Chetan Pawar told reporters that the reward was being offered in response to a similar announcement by a Shiv Sena (UBT) office-bearer from Mumbai."As everyone knows, our party office-bearer from Mumbai has already announced a reward of Rs 1 lakh for anyone who slaps Shaina NC. Shaina was also seen tearing a portion of a photograph depicting Balasaheb Thackeray striking an effigy of Congress leader Mani Shankar Aiyar with a slipper.The incident was captured on camera and drew criticism from Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders.Shaina denied deliberately disrespecting Balasaheb, maintaining that she had torn the portion showing Aiyar and not the photograph of the late Shiv Sena founder. Article Title: Brent crude falls over $1 as Trump signals fresh US strikes on Iran are unlikely
Article Text:
Crude oil eases after Trump's remarks

Trump warns Iran despite ruling out fresh strikes

Hormuz caught in chokehold

Oil prices opened lower on Monday, with Brent crude briefly shedding more than $1 a barrel.The dip comes after US President Donald Trump said that fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations between the two countries made progress.Brent crude futures fell 52 cents, or 0.53%, to $97.80 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, or 0.17%, to $90.68 a barrel.Trump's comments offered an indication that the US could avoid another round of military action against Iran, provided Tehran agreed to what he described as a strong deal. However, reports from both countries of shipping being hit in and around the Strait of Hormuz kept concerns over disruptions to the strategic waterway alive."It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement," Trump told CNN in a phone interview. "The answer is, highly unlikely it's going to be necessary."In a 20-minute telephone interview with CNN, Trump repeated five times that renewed military intervention was unlikely if Iran made tangible progress in negotiations over its nuclear programme and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.The US president, however, warned that Washington had identified 38 Iranian bridges that could be destroyed within an hour if further military action became necessary."We have 38 bridges in our site that we can knock down in literally one hour. They’ll all be down," Trump told CNN.The remarks come amid continued disruption to crude oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, which has now lasted for over eight months. The disruption has affected refinery operations across major Asian and Middle Eastern economies.According to the US Energy Information Administration (EIA), global refinery activity fell sharply in the second quarter of 2026 after the Middle East conflict broke out.Data from energy intelligence firm Kpler showed that global refinery inputs dropped by 4.8 million barrels per day (b/d), or 6%, in April-June compared with the previous quarter. However, they recovered by 1.8 million b/d in the third quarter as refiners adapted to changing trade flows and alternative supply routes.Countries that rely heavily on crude supplies passing through the Strait of Hormuz were among the worst affected.China saw the biggest decline, with refinery inputs falling by 2.1 million b/d in the second quarter and a further 0.8 million b/d in the third quarter.India, South Korea and Japan together recorded a drop of more than 1 million b/d in crude oil inputs in the second quarter. Their combined inputs recovered by 0.8 million b/d in the following quarter.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures fell 52 cents, or 0.53%, to $97.80 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, to $90.68 a barrels. US President Donald Trump said fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations between the two countries made progress.

Article Title: Sheikh Hasina seeks new passport for Bangladesh return, Dhaka says not 'to a terrorist'
Article Text:
The request is reportedly the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December

Death sentence and legal proceedings
