NEW DELHI: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID), taking a step towards her planned return from India in December.The information comes from a Monday letter sent by Hasina’s lawyers to the acting high commissioner at Bangladesh's embassy in Delhi, Preeti Rahman, Reuters reported.Hasina's lawyers at London-based Matrix Chambers requested the issuance of fresh documents. They cited the reported cancellation of her existing passport and NID by Bangladesh's interim government and other authorities."In view of the reported revocation of her existing Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card (NID) by the Interim Government and other authorities, I respectfully request that you take the necessary steps to issue a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card for our client," the lawyers wrote.The letter urged the authorities to process the applications "expeditiously", citing Hasina's Bangladeshi nationality and the country's "obligations arising under international human rights instruments".However, Bangladesh denied Hasina’s request, stating that the country does not provide "passport to a terrorist"."She is a fugitive criminal. We have an active extradition treaty with India. We want her handed over," Bangladesh state minister for foreign affairs, Humaiun Kobir, told reporters."Should we treat her like an ordinary commercial traveller and tell her ​to come and visit her ​in-laws’ residence?" Kobir jibed.According to Reuters, the request is the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December, more than two years after a deadly uprising forced her from power. Her return could reignite political and legal tensions as Bangladesh attempts to restore stability and her Awami League party remains banned.Hasina intends to return and surrender before a court. Her aides said on Monday that the date would be announced after the completion of various formalities.Last week, the exiled leader the Associated Press she would prefer dying in her own land, among her own people.“If death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” Hasina said.In November 2025, Bangladesh's war-crimes tribunal sentenced Hasina to death in absentia for ordering a crackdown on the student-led uprising. She has denied the charges, rejected the verdict and questioned the legitimacy of the trial.The crackdown killed hundreds of protesters and left thousands injured. According to United Nations data cited by the Associated Press, nearly 1,400 people were killed during the unrest.Bangladesh has repeatedly sought Hasina's extradition from India. New Delhi has said the request is being examined through legal channels.Hasina's Awami League was Bangladesh's largest political party before it was banned following her removal from office. Several of its leaders and members have since been jailed, while others have gone into self-imposed exile in India and elsewhere.Having served as Prime Minister for 20 years across multiple terms, Hasina retains support among sections of the population. Her return could deepen political divisions as the country continues to deal with the aftermath of the upheaval.It could also have implications for Bangladesh's strained relationship with India, which deteriorated sharply after New Delhi gave the former prime minister refuge.
Article Summary: Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID) The request is reportedly the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December. Bangladesh denied Hasina’s request, stating that the country does not provide "passport to a terrorist"

Article Title: As US gets ready to celebrate Thanksgiving, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton sends a 'warning'; says: American people should be ...
Article Text:
Trump has named intelligence chief Jay Clayton as his AI czar, putting him in charge of a new White House task force that will examine AI’s risks and opportunities and recommend how the US government should respond.

Americans should be prepared for disruptions

What happened

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Treasury secretary compares upgrades to a vaccine

As the Americans can preparing to travel for Thanksgiving, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton has warned that the disruptions in technology may continue as companies and government agencies are modernising their systems for the age of artificial intelligence. Appearing on CNN’s “State of the Union,” Clayton said outages may continue as companies and the government upgrade their systems to adapt to the AI era. He said the public should expect heavy investment in upgrading systems and in cybersecurity, and that any major leap in technology, in computing power or applications, brings disruption. People should understand that systems will be upgraded and may be interrupted for a time, he said, and that companies and the government are dealing with the problem proactively.Speaking on CNN's State of the Union, Clayton said the public should expect temporary interruptions as organisations invest heavily in new technologies and cybersecurity measures. "The American people should be prepared for a great deal of investment in upgrading our systems; they should be prepared for investment in cybersecurity, and they should be prepared that any time there is a step change in technology, a step change in both compute and applications, there will be bumps in the road," Clayton said, according to a CNBC report.He added that people should understand that system upgrades may occasionally result in service interruptions while both government agencies and private companies work to strengthen infrastructure and security. "You prepare by knowing that systems are going to be upgraded; they may be interrupted for a period of time and that companies and government are dealing with this on the front foot," he said.Government officials have largely dismissed the idea that the outages are linked to a coordinated cyberattack or one driven by artificial intelligence. The disruptions also slowed some bank transactions.A technology failure triggered a nationwide ground stop for flights just over a week ago that lasted for hours. The Federal Aviation Administration said router upgrades produced a flood of data that caused the stoppage, and that there is no indication of a cyberattack. Microsoft separately said its Outlook outage resulted from an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade.US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent delivered a similar message during an appearance on CBS' Face the Nation, urging Americans not to worry about the security of their financial institutions. Asked whether consumers should be concerned about banks, Bessent replied, "No, they shouldn't."Referring to software updates and security improvements designed to protect systems against emerging AI-related threats, he acknowledged that occasional glitches may occur."The patches may cause a glitch," Bessent said. "I think the American people should think of it as a vaccine; your arm may hurt, you may feel a little bad the next day, but it increases your long-term immunity and resiliency."
Article Summary: Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton says companies and government are upgrading systems for the age of artificial intelligence. Clayton said the public should expect temporary interruptions as organisations invest heavily in new technologies and cybersecurity measures. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged Americans not to worry about their financial institutions.

Article Title: Truck driver burnt alive after vehicle hits 11kV pole in Gumla
Article Text:
Gumla

:





A 35-year-old truck driver was burnt alive after his vehicle collided with a car, rammed into an 11 kV electricity pole and caught fire near Kartik Oraon College on Palkot Road on the intervening night of Monday and Tuesday, police said.The deceased was identified as Pankaj Kumar , a resident of Lalkot in Uttar Pradesh’s Hathras district.Police said the truck collided with a car while the driver was apparently trying to avoid it. The vehicle then veered off the road, hit the electricity pole and came in contact with a live power line. It caught fire and was engulfed in flames within minutes.“The driver was trapped inside the cabin after the crash and was burnt alive,” Sadar police station officer in-charge Dinesh Kumar said.A fire tender was rushed to the spot, but the truck had been completely destroyed by the time the blaze was brought under control.Ankur Kumar, who was driving another truck behind Pankaj’s vehicle, identified him. He told police both of them belonged to the same village. Pankaj was transporting iron rods from Rourkela to Aligarh, he said.According to Ankur, three people were travelling in the car, which was heading from Gumla towards Simdega.Deputy superintendent of Sadar Hospital Dr Anupam Kishore said two injured persons were brought to the hospital. “One was referred to Rims, Ranchi, while the other, who had sustained minor injuries, was discharged,” he said.Police prepared an inquest report and said the driver’s remains would be sent for postmortem examination.
Article Summary: The truck collided with a car while the driver was apparently trying to avoid it. The vehicle then veered off the road, hit the electricity pole and came in contact with a live power line. The driver was trapped inside the cabin after the crash and was burnt alive.

Article Title: 'Population growth a strategic issue, can help repel enemy threats': Iran's Mojtaba Khamenei
Article Text:
Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei (File photo)

(With ANI inputs)

Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei on Tuesday linked population growth to national strength, saying a larger young population would help the country counter the "threats and malicious intentions of the enemy".His remarks came during Iran's Fourth National Event on Population Rejuvenation."This strategic issue that helps to shape the future, which our illustrious, martyred Leader had repeatedly emphasised over the past decades, is highly effective both in actualising the nation's capacities and in creating and enhancing many opportunities in science, culture, economics, and society," a statement quoted Mojtaba Khamenei as saying. He was referring to his father and predecessor, Ali Khamenei.The Iranian Supreme Leader further claimed that population growth is also influential in "repelling and removing the threats and malicious intentions of the enemy".Mojtaba's reference to the "enemy" appeared to be aimed at the United States and its ally Israel. Ali Khamenei was killed in a US-Israeli strike in Tehran on February 28, triggering a wider war in the Middle East.In his statement, Mojtaba, whose whereabouts remain unknown, also called for population growth to be treated as a "strategic national priority"."Giving serious, comprehensive attention to facilitating marriage at a young age, ensuring individual health, which depends on multiple factors, supporting childbearing, promoting a family-centred culture and highlighting successful examples in this area are all effective steps towards making Iran stronger," he said.He also stressed the need to communicate the importance of population growth to the public, particularly young people, and called for infrastructure supporting family welfare to be made a permanent part of national planning.Mojtaba further acknowledged shortcomings in previous population policies, emphasising that correcting them and pursuing a strategy focused on increasing the young population would be crucial to Iran's future."Without a doubt, every patriotic Iranian who hopes for a bright and glorious future for this land and its people will have a strong determination and resolve to ensure the continuity of future generations of the Iranian nation in a manner befitting the New Islamic Civilisation," he said."I sincerely hope that by remedying the shortcomings arising from certain past population policies and by earnestly pursuing the sound, strategic policy of increasing the young population and placing the family at the centre of this effort, our dear homeland will safely navigate this critical juncture and stage, which it now finds itself in and which will shape the future," he added.
Article Summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei linked population growth to national strength. He said a larger young population would help the country counter the "threats and malicious intentions of the enemy" His remarks came during Iran's Fourth National Event on Population Rejuvenation.

Article Title: Man pulls blade from hair, slashes himself inside Mumbai local after being asked to vacate seat
Article Text:
Jhade attributed his actions to stress arising from family-related issues.





MUMBAI: A commuter injured himself with a blade inside a Virar-Churchgate local train on Monday evening, scaring fellow passengers who pulled the emergency chain to stop the train at Andheri station.The incident occurred after the train left Virar around 6pm. The commuter, identified as Praful Jhade, was sleeping on a seat when another passenger asked him to get up. Jhade then took out a blade kept in his hair and began slashing himself, leaving fellow commuters alarmed.The train halted at platform 7 of Andheri station at 6.56pm. Woman police constable Saraswati and Maharashtra Security Force personnel inspected the coach and found Jhade injured. He was taken to the station’s emergency medical room, where doctors administered first aid.During questioning, Jhade told railway police that he was a resident of Nagpur and was undergoing treatment for a mental health condition at JJ Hospital in Mumbai. He attributed his actions to stress arising from family-related issues.Police searched him but did not find the blade. After receiving first aid and recording his statement, Jhade left for home on his own. Railway authorities said the incident did not affect suburban train services.
Article Summary: Praful Jhade was sleeping on a seat when another passenger asked him to get up. He then took out a blade kept in his hair and began slashing himself. Fellow passengers pulled the emergency chain to stop the train at Andheri station.

Article Title: Saving tigers could cost 1.15 lakh trees: Sahyadri Tiger Reserve village relocations flagged in Maharashtra, NTCA refuses to back Nivale plan over dense forest, RTI shows felling data left blank
Article Text:
The report said no suitable non-forest land was available and that relocation would return 519.49 hectares to the forest. (AI image)

The numbers behind the relocation

Male: 227.9 hectares of forest land; 38,738 trees listed for felling.

Vele: 112.25 hectares; 2,918 trees listed.

Nivale: 63.091 hectares; 34,705 trees listed.

Kolane: 76.17 hectares; proposal questioned by the ministry.

20,071: Gliricidia trees identified among the 38,738 listed for felling.

87%: Share of trees below 60 cm in girth.

140: Families seeking relocation.

519.49 hectares: Land expected to return to the forest.





MUMBAI: Maharashtra's efforts to clear tiger-reserve core areas of human habitation to improve wildlife conservation could come at a significant ecological cost. Relocation proposals in the Sahyadri Tiger Reserve landscape have been flagged for a cumulative impact involving nearly 1.15 lakh trees.The National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) has refused to recommend one of the proposals, citing the use of dense forest for rehabilitation.Records obtained under the Right to Information (RTI) Act by Jeetendra Ghadge of the Young Whistleblowers Foundation reveal the scale of the proposed tree loss and raise questions about how the state is balancing tiger conservation with the protection of existing forest cover.The issue comes amid a renewed state push to expedite village rehabilitation. At a Maharashtra CAMPA authority meeting on October 26, the government directed that rehabilitation of villages in tiger reserves and protected areas be completed using CAMPA funds. It said 55 villages had already been relocated and sought central funding for further rehabilitation in phases.The RTI response shows that two villages in Chandoli National Park, part of the Sahyadri Tiger Reserve, received final approval for relocation-related forest land on January 29, 2024.Male was allotted 227.9 hectares, with 38,738 trees listed for felling, while Vele was allotted 112.25 hectares, involving another 2,918 trees. However, the column recording the actual number of trees felled was left blank in the department's response.A February 16, 2026, communication from the Union environment ministry raised further concerns over the proposed relocation of Nivale village. Its rehabilitation site involves 63.091 hectares of forest land at Kagal in Kolhapur district, where 34,705 trees have been listed.The NTCA refused to recommend the proposal, pointing out that the land included dense forest and that degraded forest should instead be prioritised for rehabilitation.The authority also noted that Nivale had already been relocated once and called for a cumulative impact assessment. Separately, the ministry questioned a 76.17-hectare proposal for Kolane, asking why the relocation of one village had been divided into multiple proposals.The state, however, has cited factors supporting the relocation proposal. A central inspection report on Male found that 20,071 of the 38,738 trees listed for felling were Gliricidia, a species described as invasive and originally planted to green barren land. Around 87% of the trees were below 60 cm in girth.The report said no suitable non-forest land was available and that relocation would return 519.49 hectares to the forest. It also recorded that 140 families were seeking relocation.For the affected villagers, the issue is also one of prolonged uncertainty. The Satara district administration fixed November 12, 2025, as the cut-off date to identify eligible families from Male, Kolane and Patharpunj.In May 2026, it directed the forest department to pay subsistence allowances until rehabilitation was completed. Relocation is also intended to facilitate conservation measures, including the reintroduction of tigers in the reserve.Ghadge said rehabilitation from tiger-reserve core areas was necessary but should not become a process in which one forest was sacrificed to protect another without assessing the overall ecological damage.He questioned the absence of publicly available, proposal-wise assessments explaining the cumulative impact involving nearly 1.15 lakh trees.Environmental activist Rajesh Ruparel cautioned that compensatory plantation could not automatically replace an established natural forest. Mature forests support interconnected biodiversity, wildlife habitats, soil conservation and water systems, functions that newly planted saplings cannot immediately replicate, he said.The larger unanswered questions concern transparency and ecological accountability: how many trees have actually been felled, whether native-species restoration has begun and how authorities assessed the cumulative damage against the conservation gains.The forest department and NTCA have been sent queries. Their responses were awaited.The nearly 1.15 lakh trees represent the cumulative impact flagged by the NTCA and the Union environment ministry. This is not the verified number of trees already felled.Village-wise details:What the inspection found in Male:According to the state government, 55 villages have already been relocated across Maharashtra's tiger reserves and protected areas.
Article Summary: Relocation proposals in the Sahyadri Tiger Reserve landscape have been flagged for a cumulative impact involving nearly 1.15 lakh trees. National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) has refused to recommend one of the proposals, citing the use of dense forest for rehabilitation.

Article Title: Scooter rider falls under BEST bus while overtaking, dies on the spot in Mumbai
Article Text:
(Representative) An accident involving a BEST bus and a scooter rider occurred in Kurla on Tuesday morning





MUMBAI: An unidentified scooter rider was killed in a road accident involving a BEST wet-lease bus in Kurla (West) on Tuesday morning after he allegedly fell between the vehicle's wheels while attempting to overtake it.The accident occurred around 7.10am near Budh Colony. The BEST bus, operating on route 310 from Bandra Terminus (East) to Kurla Bus Station (West), was on its regular trip when the incident took place.According to preliminary inquiries, the scooter rider attempted to overtake the bus from the right. During the manoeuvre, his two-wheeler collided with a tempo travelling ahead of the bus.The impact caused the rider to lose his balance and fall on the road between the bus's front and rear wheels. He suffered severe head injuries near the right-side rear axle and died on the spot.The bus conductor immediately alerted the police control room. Police personnel subsequently reached the accident site and shifted the body to Rajawadi Hospital for a postmortem examination and identification.Senior BEST officials and representatives of the wet-lease operator also inspected the accident spot. Vinoba Bhave Nagar police have initiated legal proceedings and are conducting further inquiries into the circumstances surrounding the accident.
Article Summary: The accident occurred around 7.10am near Budh Colony. The BEST bus, operating on route 310 from Bandra Terminus (East) to Kurla Bus Station (West) The rider suffered severe head injuries near the right-side rear axle and died on the spot.

Article Title: Replacement of hostel fan rods begins at IIT Bombay
Article Text:
IIT-B is initiating a replacement of ceiling fan rods in Hostel 4 and other hostels.





MUMBAI: Two months after the death of a student, Sahil Wakode, in Hostel 4, IIT-B has begun replacing ceiling fan rods in hostel rooms as part of a broader initiative to improve student safety on campus. The exercise, which was scheduled to begin on November 22, will be extended to other hostels in phases.In a communication to students, Aditya Joshi, general secretary of hostel affairs, said the institute was undertaking several measures to strengthen student safety and improve hostel infrastructure. These include seeking feedback from students and consulting their representatives to identify practical solutions.“The replacement work will initially be carried out in Hostel 4, with the schedule for other hostels to be communicated through their respective hostel general secretaries and maintenance councillors,” said a student, quoting the letterThe decision comes against the backdrop of the death of Wakode, a second-year BTech student in the Department of Energy Science and Engineering, who died by suicide in his Hostel 4 room on September 18.His death had triggered protests on campus, with students demanding an independent investigation and stronger mechanisms to address student grievances.
Article Summary: IIT-B has begun replacing ceiling fan rods in hostel rooms as part of a broader initiative to improve student safety on campus. The exercise, which was scheduled to begin on November 22, will be extended to other hostels in phases. Sahil Wakode, a second-year BTech student, died by suicide in his Hostel 4 room on September 18.

Article Title: ​​​Two killed, 17 injured as Nagpur-Mumbai bus overturns on Samruddhi Expressway
Article Text:
A private passenger bus that met with accident on the Samruddhi Expressway in Phulambri taluka in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on Monday

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Two passengers were killed and 17 others were injured after a private passenger bus overturned on the Samruddhi Expressway at Naygaon in Phulambri taluka of Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar in the early hours of Monday.The deceased are Raghunandan Datta Sangale (26), a resident of West Mumbai, and Vinod Uttam Jadhav, a resident of Ghonsgaon in Yavatmal’s Arni taluka, who died during treatment.The accident occurred around 1.10 am on Monday at Channel No. 426 on the expressway’s Nagpur-Mumbai corridor, as the bus driver is suspected to have dozed off during the journey, said Sonali Paikrao, in charge of Phulambri police station.“The bus, MH-41-ZH-9955, was travelling from Nagpur to Mumbai with 38 passengers. As per preliminary information, the driver dozed off, lost control of the vehicle and the bus overturned on the highway, leaving several passengers injured,” Paikrao said, adding that the case registration process against the bus driver was underway.On receiving information about the accident, highway police and a Phulambri police station team rushed to the spot and coordinated the rescue operation. Local rescue teams, ambulances and police safely pulled the passengers from the bus and shifted the injured to Govt Medical College and Hospital in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar for treatment.Police have appealed to drivers on the Samruddhi Expressway to start their journey only after adequate rest, avoid driving when feeling sleepy or tired, follow speed limits and give top priority to passenger safety.
Article Summary: The accident occurred around 1.10 am on Monday at Channel No. 426 on the expressway’s Nagpur-Mumbai corridor. The bus driver is suspected to have dozed off during the journey. The deceased are Raghunandan Datta Sangale (26), a resident of West Mumbai, and Vinod Uttam Jadhav, who died during treatment.

Article Title: BJP corporator’s minor son booked after speeding SUV kills Beed couple; police say friend was driving
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





The minor son of a BJP corporator was booked after a speeding SUV allegedly rammed a motorcycle head-on, killing a couple in Beed’s Majalgaon on Nov 20. Police, however, said a video shot inside the SUV shows the corporator’s son was not driving.The victims, Prahlad Gaikwad and his wife Sunita Gaikwad, were residents of Mangrul village near Majalgaon. According to a complaint filed by the couple’s son, the two were returning home on their motorcycle after attending a shraddha ceremony. Around 3.30 pm, near Saubhagya Mangal Karyalaya, an SUV allegedly came at high speed and hit their motorcycle head-on.Police subsequently booked the minor son of a local corporator under sections 106(1), 281 and 324(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and sections 134 and 187 of the Motor Vehicles Act. However, police said fresh evidence that emerged during the investigation indicates that the corporator’s son was not behind the wheel.Majalgaon police station in-charge Dhananjay Dhone said a video filmed inside the SUV, apparently for a reel, shows four friends in the vehicle before the crash.“It shows four friends inside the car, with the corporator’s son sitting next to his friend who was driving. The video also shows the airbags deploying after the impact. The corporator’s son was not driving. His friend was behind the wheel,” Dhone said.A section of local residents alleged that the crash was linked to road rage and illegal street racing. Police said that allegation has not been established.“The CCTV footage of the accident shows the SUV was at high speed. It is not yet clear whether any street racing was on,” Dhone said.Police are recording statements of those involved. No arrests had been made till Monday evening.The BJP corporator, meanwhile, also denied that his son was driving or that the SUV was involved in street racing. “My son’s friend was driving the car and he appeared before the police after the accident. My political rivals are trying to target me and my family after the accident,” he said.
Article Summary: The minor son of a BJP corporator was booked after a speeding SUV allegedly rammed a motorcycle head-on, killing a couple. Police, however, said a video shot inside the SUV shows the corporator’s son was not driving. A section of local residents alleged that the crash was linked to road rage and illegal street racing. Police said that allegation has not been established.

Article Title: ​Police’s own photos expose wrong e-challans issued to same family in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar
Article Text:
File photo

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Two separate incidents in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar have exposed acts of wrongful challans issued by the traffic police against members of the same family.In the first e-challan, the traffic police fined the wrong vehicle due to a wrong letter in the car number. In the other case, the police first fined a car driver for not wearing a helmet and then issued the same challan for overspeeding, even though the police speed camera showed the car was within limits.In both cases, the police’s own photographs contradict their challans, yet both fines still stand against two members of the same family from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.The first case is of a car, MH20-EY0545. An e-challan was issued against the car’s owner on Saturday for using a mobile phone while driving. However, the photograph attached as proof shows a completely different vehicle — MH20-EA0545. The difference is of one letter — Y in place of A — in the number of both cars.“I was shocked to see a message on my mobile about a traffic violation when I had not even driven the car on Saturday,” said Nityanand Zadbuke, the car owner.The second incident involved Nityanand’s elder brother, Dr Amol Zadbuke, a health professional.The owner of car number MH20-CH3609 had first received an e-challan for not wearing a helmet in Dec last year. “I was taken aback by the traffic violation. When I raised a dispute, the same challan issued last year was shown as proof of overspeeding. But police’s own speed-camera photo shows my vehicle was moving at 57 Km/hr, which is well within the permissible speed of 95 Km/ hr,” Dr Zadbuke said.When contacted, Subhash Bhujang, the assistant commissioner of police (traffic), said that complaints related to both e-challans would be examined if vehicle owners approach the traffic police.“Misreading of letters on a number plate by the technical system cannot be ruled out, as vehicles are constantly moving. The other case with Dr Zadbuke is exceptional, and official intervention will be offered if the vehicle owner is not happy with the earlier grievance redressal,” he said.
Article Summary: In the first e-challan, the traffic police fined the wrong vehicle due to a wrong letter in the car number. In the other case, the police first fined a car driver for not wearing a helmet and then issued same challan for overspeeding.
